Olivia: Heads up — SOC asked for a standard template for timeboxed analyst leases to access SIEM exports. We need RBAC + KMS unwrap + redaction. Can we agree on a minimal flow?
Sam: Yes. Quick proposal below — short and prescriptive.
Sam: ```Request template for analyst lease:
- ticket_id:
- requestor (email):
- data_scope (datasets + time window):
- delivery_method (secure-proxy | s3-presigned | airgap):
- ttl_hours (max 48):
- redaction_level (full, pii-mask, none - justify):
- approver (team + role):
- purpose / justification:
- reviewer (post-access): list logs to check for misuse
```
Maria: KMS question — should we grant analysts kms:Decrypt on CMK? we shouldn't.
Sam: No. Pattern: proxy service performs decrypt on behalf of the user after approval. Analysts never get key permissions. Proxy logs the unwrap event and stamps ticket_id.
Jamal: +1. Also require that the proxy only unwraps to ephemeral S3 with SSE-C or presigned URL that expires with TTL. No persistent buckets.
Olivia: Can we standardize TTL to 24h for most requests, 48h only with exec approval?
Sam: Yes. Default 24h, escalate to 48h requires manager + security approver.
Maria: Audit fields we need logged: ticket_id, requestor, approver, proxy-instance-id, kms-request-id, object-hash, start_ts, end_ts. Everything goes to the audit-log index.
Jamal: Also add: dataset owner must sign off if export includes raw packet-level or sensitive PII. For typical app logs, a PII-scrubbed export is default.
Olivia: Example command for the proxy (for docs):
Sam: ```bash
# internal log-proxy call (example)
log-proxy fetch --ticket 12345 \  --scope "svc=auth,from=2026-03-17T00:00,to=2026-03-18T00:00" \  --delivery presigned-s3 --ttl 24h \  --redaction pii-mask
```
Maria: Who rotates the CMK? If CMK rotates mid-lease, we need the proxy to hold unwrap metadata so we can still attribute the action.
Sam: CMK rotation is ops. Proxy stores kms-request-id and ciphertext-blob in the audit log so correlation survives rotation. We don't keep plaintext.
Jamal: One more: deny contractors and third-party vendors from raw exports by policy. Allow only pre-scrubbed views via dashboards.
Olivia: How do we handle evidence for incidents? Sometimes SecOps needs whole raw snapshot for triage. Process: emergency access with stamped short-lived lease (1-4 hours) + exec approval and post-incident review.
Sam: Right. Emergency path = same template but TTL <= 4, plus incident ticket link and SLA for post-review notes.
sec-bot: :lock: Reminder: All KMS unwraps will create a compliance event. Attach ticket to event or it will auto-reject.
Maria: I can draft PR for runbook and add the request template + proxy examples. Want me to include Terraform snippet for a proxy role?
Olivia: Yes please. Also add a sample ticket with minimal justification. Keep wording tight.
Jamal: I'll add the RBAC policy snippet to block kms:Decrypt for analyst role, and the proxy role that can assume a decrypt role.
Sam: Quick RBAC pseudo: ```json
{
  "Statement": [
    { "Effect": "Deny", "Action": "kms:Decrypt", "Principal": "arn:aws:iam::account:role/analyst" },
    { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "kms:Decrypt", "Principal": "arn:aws:iam::account:role/log-proxy" }
  ]
}
```
Olivia: Perfect. Let's aim to land the docs PR tomorrow and get SOC signoff end of week.
Sam: I'll open the PR and ping you. :eyes:
Maria: tagging infra to review proxy IAM and ensure logs are shipped to audit index.
Jamal: lgtm, can we add an example of a redaction policy for email/phone? small follow-up.
Olivia: Good call. Follow-up ticket created: https://tickets.internal/INC-2026-442.
